title: Bioinformatics Analysis of Metagenomic Sequencing Data
author: Rosa Leon

materials: MaxBin is a software for binning assembled metagenomic sequences based on an Expectation-Maximization algorithm. Users provide the assembled metagenomic sequences and the reads coverage information or sequencing reads. MaxBin will report genome-related statistics, including estimated completeness, GC content and genome size in the binning summary page. MaxBin article - https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/32/4/605/1744462 perl /storage/BioInfo_tools/MaxBin-2.2.4/run_MaxBin.pl -contig "assembled_contigs.fa" -reads "reads file" -reads2 "readsfile" -out "out directory" -thread 5 MaxBin requires the assembled contains file and also the file that contains the sequence readsassembled_contigs.fa = your contigs file (remember to add the full path if you are in a different directory)reads = the path to your reads ( or paired R1 followed by R2 reads). out directory = a directory that you create to save your bins perl /opt/BioInfo_tools/MaxBin-2.2.4/run_MaxBin.pl -contig "assembled_contigs.fa" -reads "interleaved reads fasta" -out "out directory" -thread 5 MaxBin requires the assembled contains file and also the file that contains the sequence reads assembled_contigs.fa = your contigs file (remember to add the full path if you are in a different directory) concatenated reads fasta = the path to your reads, these reads most all be in one file and concatenate ( or paired R1 followed by R2 reads). This you can get from your IDBA fq2fa run out directory = a directory that you create to save your bins
Convert quality scores to Phred-33 TOPHRED

VizBin is a java software that calculates kmer composition and creats a pictographical output that shows the similatity between contigs realted to how close they are postition to each other. We will use VizBin to help us de-contaminate out bins VizBin will generate a visualization window. Each point represents a genomic fragment (by default of length >= 1,000nt). VizBin is designed with the user in mind. All that is needed is a fasta file containing the sequences of interest. A step-by-step guide on using VizBin - including a description of loading the data, selecting points, and exporting the sequences represented by the selected points - is provided on the tutorial page of VizBin's github wiki In order to run VizBin with you data you must download you bins fasta files onto your desktop. To download go to the VizBin page

Phylosift software searches for single copy marker genes and finds thier taxonomic classification Before running this command take a moment to learn about the sorftware at the Phylosift webpage /usr/local/phylosift_v1.0.1/bin/phylosift all your_bin.fasta --threads 3 To run Phylosfit you only need to have change your_bin.fasta for the files (and path if required) for each of your individual bins

steps.title: Set up and run FastQC
steps.instruction: Create an alias for FastQC (alias fastqc=/storage/BioInfo_tools/FastQC/fastqc), then run fastqc on each .fastq or .fastq.gz file (e.g., fastqc seqfile1.fastq). Transfer the FastQC output folder from the server with scp -r username@bio-server-2.willamette.edu:/home/username/folder_with_fastqc_file ~/Desktop/. Unzip the result folder locally and open the .html summary file in a browser to assess read quality.

steps.title: Trim reads with Trimmomatic
steps.instruction:
Run Trimmomatic PE mode with 5 threads and Phred‑33 quality conversion using the command:
java -jar /storage/BioInfo_tools/Trimmomatic-0.36/trimmomatic-0.36.jar PE -threads 5 -phred33 input_forward.fq.gz input_reverse.fq.gz output_forward_paired.fq.gz output_forward_unpaired.fq.gz output_reverse_paired.fq.gz output_reverse_unpaired.fq.gz ILLUMINACLIP:/opt/BioInfo_tools/Trimmomatic-0.36/adapters/TruSeq3-PE.fa:2:30:10 LEADING:15 TRAILING:15 SLIDINGWINDOW:4:15 MINLEN:36
where input_forward.fq.gz = your R1 file (e.g., L6_R1_subset.fastq) and input_reverse.fq.gz = your R2 file (e.g., L6_R2_subset.fastq). First run with SLIDINGWINDOW:4:15, record the percentage of output reads, then repeat with SLIDINGWINDOW:4:30 and record the new percentage.

steps.title: Assemble metagenome using Megahit
steps.instruction:
Execute Megahit with 5 threads on the trimmed paired reads:
/storage/BioInfo_tools/megahit/megahit -1 file_R1.fq.gz -2 file_R2.fq.gz -o megahit_out -t 5
where file_R1.fq.gz and file_R2.fq.gz are the trimmed forward and reverse reads. Do not create the output folder beforehand; Megahit will do it. If a run fails and leaves an empty megahit_out folder, delete it first (rm -r megahit_out or rmdir megahit_out) before re‑running.

steps.title: Assess assembly with QUAST
steps.instruction:
Run QUAST (MetaQUAST) on the assembled contigs:
/storage/BioInfo_tools/quast/metaquast.py contig.fa --gene-finding -t 5
Replace contig.fa with the fasta file produced by Megahit (e.g., megahit_out/final.contigs.fa).

steps.title: Prepare environment for CheckM
steps.instruction:
Add the pplacer directory to your PATH by editing ~/.bashrc. Open the file with nano .bashrc, add the line:
export PATH="/storage/anaconda3/bin:$PATH"
(or, if using the alternative location, export PATH="/opt/anaconda3/bin:$PATH")
Save with Ctrl+O, exit with Ctrl+X, then log out and log back in so the change takes effect.

steps.title: Run CheckM lineage workflow
steps.instruction:
Execute CheckM on all bins (each bin must be a .fasta file) with 5 threads:
/usr/bin/checkm lineage_wf -x fasta ./bins_folder ./checkm_out_folder -t 5
where ./bins_folder is the directory containing the bin .fasta files and ./checkm_out_folder is the desired output directory.

steps.title: Generate CheckM quality table
steps.instruction:
From within the CheckM output directory, run:
/usr/bin/checkm qa lineage.ms . -o 2
Copy the generated table into Excel for further analysis before proceeding to downstream tools such as VizBin.

steps.title: Add NCBI BLAST to PATH
steps.instruction:
Edit ~/.bashrc again (nano .bashrc) and append:
export PATH="$PATH:/opt/ncbi-blast-2.7.1+/bin/"
Save (Ctrl+O), exit (Ctrl+X), and relogin so the BLAST executables become available.

steps.title: Annotate contigs with Prokka
steps.instruction:
First ensure Prokka’s bin directory is in your PATH:
export PATH=$PATH:/opt/BioInfo_tools/prokka-1.11/bin/
Then run Prokka on the assembled contigs:
/opt/BioInfo_tools/prokka-1.11/bin/prokka final.contigs.fa
(Replace final.contigs.fa with the appropriate fasta file, e.g., megahit_out/final.contigs.fa).

steps.title: Analyze proteins with KEGG BlastKOALA
steps.instruction: Open the KEGG BlastKOALA web portal (http://www.kegg.jp/blastkoala/). Upload or paste the PROKKA.faa file generated by Prokka, provide your email address, and submit the job. After receiving the confirmation email, formally submit the job, wait for completion, then download the detailed results (View → Download details). Also click the “Reconstruct Modules” link to obtain pathway reconstructions, and save the information as text or PDF (Safari recommended).

steps.title: Compare proteins to COG database
steps.instruction:
Run rpsblast against the COG database:
rpsblast -query PROKKA.faa_file -db /opt/BioInfo_tools/Cog -out output_file.out -evalue 0.00001 -outfmt "6 qseqid sseqid evalue pident score qstart qend sstart send length slen" -max_target_seqs 1
Then parse the results with the provided Perl script:
perl /opt/BioInfo_tools/cdd2cog.pl -r output_file.out -c /opt/BioInfo_tools/COG/cddid.tbl -f /opt/BioInfo_tools/COG/fun.txt -w /opt/BioInfo_tools/COG/whog -a

steps.title: Run Phylosift via tmux
steps.instruction:
Start a new tmux session:
tmux new -s phylosft_3B
Inside the session, execute Phylosift on paired reads:
/usr/local/phylosift_v1.0.1/bin/phylosift all --paired R1.fastq R2.fastq
Check that the job is running with tmux ls. Detach from the session by pressing Ctrl+b then z (as described). Re‑attach later with:
tmux a -t phylosft_3B
If the job must be terminated, kill the session:
tmux kill-session -t phylosft_3B

steps.title: Annotate full metagenome with Prokka and COG
steps.instruction: Using the final_contigs.fa file from the Megahit assembly, repeat the Prokka annotation command (step 9) and the COG comparison command (step 11), substituting the input fasta name with final_contigs.fa.
